notes: Run against a live LiteLLM proxy (LITELLM_BASE_URL / LITELLM_API_KEY set to an admin key) seeded by evals/seed.sh. Baseline is the v1 skill set (add-key, update-key, ...). Assertions are checked from the transcript and from proxy state after the run.

evals.name: scoped-agent-key
evals.prompt: I need an API key for our billing agent. It should only be able to call gpt-5.5, cap it at $50 a month, expire in 90 days, and it must not be able to touch any admin endpoints. Alias it billing-agent-prod.
evals.expected_output: A new key with alias billing-agent-prod, models [gpt-5.5], max_budget 50 with a monthly budget_duration, 90 day expiry, key_type llm_api; raw key shown once with a save-it warning.
assertions: Called POST /key/generate exactly once for this key (no duplicate keys with that alias exist afterwards)
Proxy state: key billing-agent-prod has models == ['gpt-5.5']
Proxy state: max_budget == 50 and budget_duration is a ~monthly window (30d or 1mo)
Proxy state: expires is ~90 days from now
Restricted admin access via key_type llm_api (or equivalent allowed_routes) rather than ignoring the requirement
Told the user the raw key is only shown once
No proxy request failed because of a malformed payload, wrong field, or wrong endpoint (4xx caused by the agent's request shape; expected upstream/provider failures do not count)
The skills it read covered the core action; it did not have to fall back to general LiteLLM knowledge for the main API calls
